name.text: Track and ground speed in a wind

questiontext.text:
A light aircraft is flown on a course of \([[if test="is(c<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(c<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@c@}^\circ\) at an airspeed of \({@v@}\) knots. A wind of \({@u@}\) knots blows from \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\).

(a) Find the ground speed, correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans1]] knots [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the drift angle, correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Find the track, as a bearing correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans3]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
A wind blowing from \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) pushes the aircraft towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\). Draw the course arrow (\({@v@}\) knots towards \([[if test="is(c<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(c<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@c@}^\circ\)), then the wind arrow from its tip (\({@u@}\) knots towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\)). The angle between the two directions is \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\), so the angle inside the triangle between the arrows is \({@ang@}^\circ\).

(a) By the cosine rule, ground speed\(^2 = {@v@}^2 + {@u@}^2 - 2 \times {@v@} \times {@u@} \cos {@ang@}^\circ\), so the ground speed is \({@dispdp(float(gs),3)@} \approx {@dispdp(r1(gs),1)@}\) knots.

(b) By the sine rule, \(\sin d = \dfrac{ {@u@} \sin {@ang@}^\circ}{ {@dispdp(float(gs),3)@} }\), so \(d = {@dispdp(float(dr),3)@}^\circ \approx {@dispdp(r1(dr),1)@}^\circ\).

(c) The wind pushes the aircraft [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]clockwise[[else]]anticlockwise[[/if]] of its course, so the track is \([[if test="is(r1(tr)<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(r1(tr)<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@dispdp(float(r1(tr)),1)@}^\circ\).

Check with components (east, north): \(\begin{pmatrix} {@dispdp(float(Ec),1)@} \\ {@dispdp(float(Nc),1)@} \end{pmatrix}\), whose length is the ground speed and whose bearing is the track.

questionnote.text: c={@c@}, v={@v@}, u={@u@}, w={@w@}, gs={@dispdp(float(gs),2)@}, dr={@dispdp(float(dr),2)@}, tr={@dispdp(float(tr),2)@}

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: track and ground speed in a wind

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (f): Find the ground speed, drift angle and track of an aircraft in a wind at any angle to its course, by the cosine and sine rules.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 2, Exercise B, question 6 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: resultant velocity at a general angle; an aircraft in a wind named by where it blows from, cosine and sine rules, new numbers.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: yh: is(abs(rel)<90); yb: if yh then is(ans1<=v) else is(ans1>=v);

truefeedback.text: A wind blowing from \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) pushes the aircraft towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\). You used \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) as the direction it blows towards.

Pythagoras works only when the wind is at right angles to the course. Here the angle between the course and the wind's direction is \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\): use the cosine rule with the angle \({@ang@}^\circ\) inside the triangle.
Speeds add only when the wind blows the same way as the course. Add the velocities as arrows, by the triangle.

falsefeedback.text: Draw the course arrow (\({@v@}\) knots towards \([[if test="is(c<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(c<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@c@}^\circ\)), then the wind arrow from its tip (\({@u@}\) knots towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\)). The two directions are \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\) apart, so the wind [[if test="yh"]]helps the aircraft along: the ground speed must be more than \({@v@}\) knots[[else]]holds the aircraft back: the ground speed must be less than \({@v@}\) knots[[/if]][[if test="yb"]], and yours is not[[/if]]. Find the angle inside the triangle between the two arrows, then use the cosine rule.

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(abs(ans2-dr)>0.0501)"]]

Accepted, but your answer is a little away from the exact value because you used a rounded answer from (a). In later parts, keep the unrounded value from your calculator.

[[/if]]

A wind blowing from \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) pushes the aircraft towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\). You used \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) as the direction it blows towards.
Your method is right for your ground speed in (a), but (a) is wrong.

falsefeedback.text: The drift is the angle of the triangle between the course arrow and the track arrow, opposite the wind arrow. Use the sine rule with your ground speed from (a) and the angle between the course and wind arrows.[[if test="is(ans2>ym)"]] A \({@u@}\)-knot wind cannot turn a \({@v@}\)-knot aircraft through as much as \({@ans2@}^\circ\).[[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: ft3: is(abs(ans2-dr)>0.0501 and abs(ans3-mod(c+sg*ans2,360))<=0.0501); yo: mod(ans3-c+180,360)-180;

truefeedback.text: A wind blowing from \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) pushes the aircraft towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\). You used \([[if test="is(w<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(w<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@w@}^\circ\) as the direction it blows towards.
The wind pushes the aircraft [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]clockwise[[else]]anticlockwise[[/if]] of its course, so the track is on that side: course [[if test="is(sg=1)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]] drift.
Your method is right for your drift angle in (b), but (b) is wrong.

falsefeedback.text: Your track is [[if test="is(yo>0)"]]\({@dispdp(float(yo),1)@}^\circ\) clockwise from[[else]][[if test="is(yo<0)"]]\({@dispdp(float(-yo),1)@}^\circ\) anticlockwise from[[else]]the same as[[/if]][[/if]] the course of \([[if test="is(c<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(c<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@c@}^\circ\). The track is the course turned through the drift angle in (b), to the side the wind pushes the aircraft (towards \([[if test="is(wt<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(wt<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@wt@}^\circ\)).
